answer_text:
Interpreting the final \(\neq 0\) in the usual polynomial sense, i.e. “not the zero polynomial,” let \(p\) be a nonzero polynomial.

Let \(\deg p=n\). If \(n\le 1\), then \(p'(x)p''(x)\equiv 0\), so \(p(2x)\equiv 0\), forcing \(p\equiv 0\), which is not allowed. Thus \(n\ge 2\).

Compare degrees:

\[
\deg p(2x)=n,
\]
while
\[
\deg(p'(x)p''(x))=(n-1)+(n-2)=2n-3.
\]

Therefore equality forces

\[
n=2n-3 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad n=3.
\]

So write

\[
p(x)=ax^3+bx^2+cx+d,\qquad a\ne 0.
\]

Then

\[
p(2x)=8ax^3+4bx^2+2cx+d,
\]

and

\[
p'(x)=3ax^2+2bx+c,\qquad p''(x)=6ax+2b.
\]

Thus

\[
p'(x)p''(x)
=(3ax^2+2bx+c)(6ax+2b)
\]

\[
=18a^2x^3+18abx^2+(4b^2+6ac)x+2bc.
\]

Equating coefficients with \(p(2x)\) gives

\[
8a=18a^2,
\]
\[
4b=18ab,
\]
\[
2c=4b^2+6ac,
\]
\[
d=2bc.
\]

From \(8a=18a^2\) and \(a\ne 0\),

\[
a=\frac49.
\]

Then

\[
4b=18\cdot \frac49 b=8b
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad b=0.
\]

Next,

\[
2c=6ac=6\cdot\frac49 c=\frac83 c
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad c=0.
\]

Finally,

\[
d=2bc=0.
\]

Hence the only nontrivial solution is

\[
p(x)=\frac49 x^3.
\]

Check:

\[
p(2x)=\frac49(2x)^3=\frac{32}{9}x^3,
\]

and

\[
p'(x)=\frac43x^2,\qquad p''(x)=\frac83x,
\]

so

\[
p'(x)p''(x)=\frac43x^2\cdot \frac83x=\frac{32}{9}x^3.
\]

Thus

\[
\boxed{p(x)=\frac49x^3}
\]
